seo.title: Show the robot’s job before hardware | DHEE
seo.description: Help buyers and stakeholders understand a robotics use case with a clear, illustrative product story before a hardware decision.

hero.title: Show the robot’s job
hero.body: Turn a robotics use case into a story people can follow: the task, the environment, the robot’s role and the question to validate next.
hero.imageAlt: Illustrative robot arm and mobile robot working in a clean concept environment; not a validated simulation.

concept.eyebrow: Make the idea visible before the build.
concept.title: Give the team something concrete to review.
concept.body: A focused visual demo can help a buyer, operator or internal team discuss what a robot is meant to do. It can clarify the proposed workflow and surface questions for engineering—without claiming to prove performance or replace simulation.

research.body: Start with one clearly bounded robot task and the decision the viewer needs to make.

journey.eyebrow: From task brief to next decision
journey.title: Follow the robot’s job.
journey.body: A good first demo keeps the use case specific: what the robot encounters, what action it takes and what the team still needs to validate.
journey.storyLabel: ONE ROBOT TASK / THREE CLEAR MOMENTS

steps.title: Start with the work to be done.
steps.copy: Name the task, the setting and the people or systems around it. A clear boundary keeps the story useful and avoids implying the robot can do more than intended.
steps.imageAlt: Illustrative mobile robot approaching a marked work area in a warehouse concept scene.

steps.title: Make the intended interaction visible.
steps.copy: Show the approach, interaction and handoff as a concept sequence. Use approved product references and label assumptions so reviewers can separate the story from verified capability.
steps.imageAlt: Illustrative robotic arm handling a tote at a work cell; concept visualization, not performance evidence.

steps.title: End with what the team must confirm.
steps.copy: Turn open questions into a next step: environment constraints, safety review, cycle-time targets, integration needs or a simulation and hardware test.
steps.imageAlt: Illustrative engineering review board showing a robot task, boundary markers and validation checklist.

trigger.eyebrow: A timely reason to improve the experience
trigger.title: Digital instructions are becoming part of the machinery conversation.
trigger.body: From 20 January 2027, the EU Machinery Regulation (EU) 2023/1230 allows instructions for use to be supplied digitally if its conditions are met. They must clearly identify the model, be accessible, downloadable and printable, and stay online for the machine’s expected lifetime and at least 10 years. Paper instructions can be requested at purchase; essential safety information for non-professional use has additional paper requirements. Video can support understanding, but it does not replace required instructions or establish compliance.

faqs.question: Does a concept video prove the robot can do the task?
faqs.answer: No. A concept video communicates an intended use case. It is not a validated simulation, test result, safety case or guarantee of performance.

faqs.question: What does “demo before hardware” mean here?
faqs.answer: It means making the proposed task and workflow easier to discuss before a hardware decision. It does not mean replacing feasibility work, simulation, testing or an engineering review.

faqs.question: What should we provide for a first concept?
faqs.answer: A task description, intended environment, approved product images or models, known constraints, target audience, brand references and any claims the technical team has approved.

faqs.question: Can the story use a real robot or product?
faqs.answer: Yes, when you provide approved references and your team reviews the storyboard and final output. If references are incomplete, the visuals should be labeled as illustrative.

faqs.question: Can it show safety behavior or cycle time?
faqs.answer: Only when the behavior and numbers are supported by approved product data and reviewed by your engineering and safety teams. A concept visual alone cannot establish compliance or performance.

faqs.question: Who handles revisions and production?
faqs.answer: DHEE can prepare the page and video concept, review it with your team and manage agreed revisions. The current offer is a managed production workflow, not a client-operated generation account.

cta.title: Which robot task should we make clear first?
cta.body: Bring one use case, the intended audience and the question your team needs to answer next. We can shape a focused concept for review.

footer.disclosure: Robotics visuals on this page are illustrative concepts, not validated simulations or claims of performance. Product capability, integration, safety and compliance require review by qualified engineering teams.
